text: As of Sep 2026: Phase 1A about 82% complete, target 31 Oct 2026; Phase 1B to add eight galleries and a lighthouse museum.

Born at Tallapaka village (Rajampet mandal) – historically Cuddapah (Kadapa) district (APPSC 2012 key). The area went to the new Annamayya district (named after him) in April 2022 and, with the Rajampet division, back to YSR Kadapa district from 1 Jan 2026 (as of 2026).

In Andhra the non-Brahmin current stayed mostly with the Justice Party and rationalist writers; Periyar's Dravidian separatism found little support among Telugus.

Ages ladder: consent 10 (IPC 1860) → 12 (1891) → 14 (1925) → 16 (1949) → 18 (POCSO 2012 / BNS); marriage 14/18 (1872, 1929) → 18/21 (1978 amendment; Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006). The 2021 proposal to raise women's age to 21 is not law (as of 2026).

Governor S. Abdul Nazeer, CM N. Chandrababu Naidu (as of 2026).

Current link: the rare life-size stucco sculpture came from a Buddhist site in Telangana (Phanigiri).
Unifier: brought the whole Telugu area under one rule after the Satavahanas (1199 PYQ ×2), from Ganjam to Kanchi – the Kakatiya who ruled all Andhradesa as one sovereign (APPSC 2003).
Latest: the Golconda Blue diamond (23.24 ct, fancy vivid blue, pear-shaped) was in the news in May 2025; Machilipatnam port works revive the old Gilakaladindi port.

Presented by the President of India; run by the Directorate of Film Festivals/NFDC.

AP State Housing Corporation: Weaker Section Housing Programme – "Housing for All"; current policy: house sites of 3 cents rural / 2 cents urban.

Exam angle: Maastricht created the EU; Croatia latest member; Brexit = Article 50; Euro not in circulation in 1999.
London Declaration 1949; Secretariat London; Secretary-General: Shirley Ayorkor Botchwey (Ghana).
Economic blocs by founding year: COMECON 1949 → ASEAN 1967 → APEC 1989 → NAFTA 1994 (latest of these; replaced by USMCA 2020).
Current chair: Bangladesh (from April 2025).
No permanent secretariat; annual rotating presidency. Troika: previous + current + next presidencies; 2022 = Indonesia, Italy, India.
Membership gives access to the latest nuclear technologies; it does not make a country an NPT member (UPSC 2018: only statement I correct).

UNSC creates and ends missions by resolution; Department of Peace Operations manages them; head = Under-Secretary-General Jean-Pierre Lacroix (since 2017, succeeded Hervé Ladsous; still in post 2026).

NIA Directors General: first Radha Vinod Raju; Dinkar Gupta (Jun 2022 – Mar 2024) → Sadanand Date (2024 – Jan 2026) → Rakesh Aggarwal (from 15 Jan 2026, current). (PMF Polity Part 4, src/polity/pmf-polity-04.txt p.32)

Coast Guard year: interim service from 1 Feb 1977; formally constituted by the Coast Guard Act, 18 Aug 1978 → match questions use 1978. (Praveen CA-360 Feb 2026, src/current-affairs/praveen-ca360-2026-02-magazine.txt p.140)

NCC (National Cadet Corps): voluntary tri-services youth organisation under the Ministry of Defence; NCC Act 1948 (H.N. Kunzru Committee); headed by a Director General, HQ New Delhi; motto "Unity and Discipline". (PMF LENS Apr 2026, src/current-affairs/pmf-lens-2026-04-07.txt p.7)
Independent bodies: ECI, CAG, UPSC, SPSCs.

Prominent federal features asked: division of powers, independent judiciary, supremacy of the Constitution – "allocation of financial resources" is not listed as one (APPSC G2 Prelims 2017); the Finance Commission, integrated judiciary and emergency powers are not "the" federal feature (Sachivalayam: division of powers).
⚠ Not Sachchidananda Sinha, K.M. Munshi, Alladi or M.C. Setalvad (Setalvad = first Attorney General).
"Deshratna": popular title of Dr Rajendra Prasad (Assembly President, first President of India).
Statement angle (Raj PCS 2023): final session 24 Jan 1950 ✓ and Prasad declared elected President of India in it ✓ → both correct.

Language – Munshi-Ayyangar formula (14 Sep 1949): Hindi in Devanagari as official language of the Union, English continued for 15 years, 14 other languages in the Eighth Schedule – not an immediate end of English.
Original: 395 Articles, 22 Parts, 8 Schedules → now about 470 Articles, 25 Parts, 12 Schedules (as of 2026).
Covers: Union and State ministers; candidates for and members of Parliament and State legislatures; Judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts; the CAG.

"Bear true faith and allegiance … uphold the sovereignty and integrity of India … perform the duties of my office without fear or favour … uphold the Constitution and the laws" = Form IV – Judges of the Supreme Court (incl. the Chief Justice of India) and the CAG. The President's oath says "preserve, protect and defend"; an MP's "faithfully discharge the duty".
Latest enacted amendment as of 2026: 106th (2023) – women's reservation (Arts. 239AA, 330A, 332A, 334A); no amendment has added a Part or Schedule since 2011.
Citizen-only offices: President, Vice-President, SC/HC judges, Governor, Attorney General, Advocate General.
Most times: Manipur – 11 (latest Feb 2025), then Uttar Pradesh – 10.

Status today: in Dr Balram Singh v. Union of India (25 Nov 2024) the Supreme Court upheld 'Socialist' and 'Secular' and dismissed the challenges to their insertion (as of 2026; the words were again debated politically in Jul 2025).
Not guaranteed: bail as of right, trial by jury. CrPC Secs. 50, 57 → BNSS Secs. 47, 58. Vihaan Kumar v. State of Haryana (2025): grounds must be meaningfully communicated to every arrestee.

Asked as: "At present, the right to property is a…" (legal right – APPSC AEE 2012, AMVI; UPPCS 1992, 1996; UKPSC 2021; MPPSC 2025), "Which Article?" (300A – APPSC, AD Economics), UPSC 2005 statements (only "legal right, not FR" correct: Art. 301 is trade; 300A came from the Janata government).
Number: 10 duties in 1976 (clauses a–j – the "10 commandments") → 11 at present; the 11th duty, 51A(k), added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002 (not 87th, 96th or "2001").
Latest enacted amendment (as of Nov 2026): the 106th (2023), women's reservation; the 129th and 130th are pending Bills and the 131st Bill was defeated (Apr 2026).
The 106th (2023) is the latest enacted amendment (as of Nov 2026).
Latest: Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024 (One Nation One Election, new Art. 82A) – with the JPC (as of 2026).
129th Amendment Bill, 2024 (simultaneous polls), JPC: ex-CJI B.R. Gavai – no violation of basic structure; ex-CJIs U.U. Lalit and Sanjiv Khanna raised doubts (as of 2026).

Article 63: "There shall be a Vice-President of India" – the second-highest office (second highest dignitary) after the President; modelled on the American Vice-President, but unlike the US VP he does not succeed to the Presidency for the rest of the term – he only acts until a new President enters office.

Articles 64 and 89(1): the VP is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Council of States) – the VP presides over the sessions of the Rajya Sabha. Not the President, PM, Speaker, Deputy Speaker, CJI, CEC or Leader of Opposition; the Chairman is not separately elected, appointed or nominated.
Elected, not appointed – the only one of VP / PM / Governor / CEC who is not appointed by the President.
Union Civil Aviation Minister: Ajit Singh (RLD, Dec 2011 – May 2014) when asked; now K. Rammohan Naidu (since 10 June 2024; as of 2026).

If both offices are vacant (e.g. the acting VP resigns), the Chief Justice of India (then the senior-most SC judge) discharges the President's functions – President (Discharge of Functions) Act, 1969.
On the President's resignation, the VP immediately informs the Speaker of the Lok Sabha (Art. 56(2)).
YSR Congress in the RS: 9 members after the June 2022 polls (so 9 as of July 2023); 11 after Feb 2024; fell after the 2024 resignations.
Never Speaker: K.V.K. Sundaram (he was the 2nd Chief Election Commissioner); also never: K.M. Munshi, U.N. Dhebar, P.D. Tandon, S. Radhakrishnan.

Indian Parliamentary Group (IPG): an autonomous body (1949); all MPs may be members, former MPs may become associate members; Speaker = ex officio President; Deputy Speaker and Deputy Chairman = ex officio Vice-Presidents; Secretary-General of the LS = its Secretary-General.

Warrant of Precedence: 1 President, 2 VP, 3 PM, 4 Governor within his State, 5 former Presidents (5A Deputy PM), 6 CJI and Speaker of the Lok Sabha, 7 Cabinet Ministers – so a Governor (in his State) ranks above the Speaker, and the Speaker ranks above all Cabinet Ministers except the PM.

Art. 98(3): until such a law, the President, after consultation with the Speaker (or the Chairman for the RS), makes the rules; individual appointment orders are issued by the Speaker / Secretary-General.
Head: Secretary-General of each House – appointed by the presiding officer; rank of the Cabinet Secretary. The idea of a separate legislative secretariat was raised in 1926 by Vithalbhai Patel.
Presidential election returning officer: the Secretary-General of the Lok Sabha or of the Rajya Sabha, by rotation (appointed by the ECI).
Deputy Speaker: elected by the LS from its members (Art. 93) on a date fixed by the Speaker (Rule 8), communicated to members by the Secretary-General.

Vacancy: the LS Deputy Speaker's post has been vacant since June 2019 – through the whole 17th and the 18th Lok Sabha (as of 2026); in the States, Jharkhand's post was vacant for 21 years (June 2026). Last LS Deputy Speaker: M. Thambidurai (2014-19).
Leave needs the support of at least 50 members; written notice to the Secretary-General; no reasons need be stated.

Rule 377 – matters a day: 20 in most books and keys (RAS 2018 key; PRS primer: "presently 20 MPs are allowed to raise matters under Rule 377 per day", one matter per member per week); NextGen Rocket says it was raised to 30 a day in 2015 (not found in Lok Sabha / PRS sources) – answer 20 unless 30 alone is offered.

Withdrawal from the CFI: authorisation must come from Parliament (an Appropriation Act) – not the President, PM, Finance Minister or CAG. In India the CAG has no "comptroller" power over issue of money; the Ministries draw under the Appropriation Act.
CAG audits all three funds of the Union and the States.
CAG – salary, allowances, pension and office expenses (Art. 148).
Latest: the LS approved the second batch of Supplementary Demands for Grants 2025-26 (Art. 115).

Function: examines the Appropriation Accounts, Finance Accounts and the CAG's audit reports – the financial accounts of the Government; checks that money was spent "within the scope of the demand"; looks at waste, loss and nugatory expenditure.
"Watchdog" on departmental expenditure and irregularities; the CAG is its "guide, friend and philosopher" and assists it.
Reports: submitted to the Speaker / Lok Sabha (i.e. to Parliament; a copy laid in the RS) – not the President, PM, FM or CAG.
Limits: examines estimates only after they are voted; cannot question policy laid down by Parliament; no CAG assistance; advisory.
Chairmen asked: Ummareddy Venkateswarlu (1999-2004, 13th LS); Sanjay Jaiswal (18th LS, as of 2026).
Examines reports and accounts of public undertakings and the CAG's reports on them; whether they run on sound business principles; not major policy or day-to-day administration.

Currently before JPCs (2026): Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024 (One Nation One Election); FCRA (Amendment) Bill, 2026; Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhisthan Bill, 2025 (a JPC, not a single-House select committee).
After bifurcation the residuary AP has 175 Assembly constituencies (not 180, 185, 195 or 150); this was also the strength "as on May 2020" (elected members).
Giani Zail Singh (President 1982-87) served as Secretary-General (head) of the Non-Aligned Movement, 1983-86, after India hosted the 7th NAM summit (New Delhi, 1983).
Returning Officer: the Election Commission appoints the Secretary-General of the Lok Sabha or of the Rajya Sabha, by rotation (Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Act, 1952) – not the CEC.
Resignation: addressed to the Vice-President, who communicates it to the Speaker of the Lok Sabha (not to the CJI, PM, RS Chairman or the electoral college).
Union executive: President, Vice-President, Prime Minister, Council of Ministers and Attorney General (Part V, Chapter I) – not the Speaker or the RS Deputy Chairman.

Reports laid before Parliament by the President: Finance Commission recommendations (Art. 281), CAG reports (Art. 151), National Commission for SCs (Art. 338), UPSC, Linguistic Minorities – but not the PAC report (a committee of Parliament itself).

Both offices vacant: the Chief Justice of India, and in his absence the senior-most SC judge, discharges the President's functions – President (Discharge of Functions) Act, 1969 – not the PM, Speaker, AG or CEC.

Article 76: office of the Attorney General (AG) for India – the highest (first) law officer of the country; appointed by the President (not by Parliament, the Speaker, the PM or on Parliament's recommendation). Not Arts. 77, 78 or 79.

Article 88: though not a member, he may speak and take part in the proceedings of either House, a joint sitting and any committee of which he is named a member – without a right to vote. So he is the non-member who can participate in Lok Sabha proceedings (not the CJI, the Vice-President, the Solicitor General, the CAG or a Governor).
R. Venkataramani – AG since 1 October 2022 (after K.K. Venugopal); re-appointed for two years from 1 October 2025 (as of 2026).

Cabinet Secretary: the senior-most / highest civil servant (bureaucrat) of the Union – not the Home Secretary, the PM's Secretary, the Lok Sabha Secretary-General, a Chief Secretary or the Attorney General (a law officer, not a civil servant). "First among equals" among Secretaries; 11th in the Table of Precedence; chairs the Civil Services Board.
Eight Cabinet Committees (as of April 2025); not PM-chaired: Parliamentary Affairs and Accommodation.
So the Telugu State had been under President's Rule twice as of 2004 (1954-55 and 1973). The 1984 Nadendla episode was not President's Rule.
Droupadi Murmu – first woman Governor of Jharkhand (2015-21); President of India from 2022.
Places the CAG report on the State, the SPSC report and the State Finance Commission report before the Legislature.
N. Chandrababu Naidu – CM again since 12 June 2024 (TDP-led NDA); K. Pawan Kalyan Deputy CM (as of 2026).

Appointed by: the Governor under Article 164(1) (not Art. 163, 165 or 166; not the President, a High Court judge or the Attorney General). Other Ministers are appointed by the Governor on the CM's advice.
Attorney General (AG) of India = the highest law officer of the country and the first law officer / chief legal adviser of the Government of India (Art. 76).
Distractors: the Chief Justice of India heads the judiciary, the Law Minister looks after legal matters in the Cabinet, the Solicitor General is only the second law officer, the CAG is the auditor.
Only the AG (Union) and the Advocate General (State) are constitutional law officers; the Solicitor General and Additional Solicitors General are not mentioned in Art. 76.
Only the AG among the listed officers has this right: not the Solicitor General, CJI, CEC, CAG, Finance Commission chairman, NHRC chairman or National Security Adviser.

Asked as: statements on the AG (Group-II Mains 2025 "only I and II"; UPPSC 2020 "only I"); "holds office during the pleasure of the Parliament" = the wrong one (APPSC Welfare Officers Mains); who holds office during the President's pleasure (AG, not CAG/CEC/Speaker – UPPSC 2016); "President cannot remove the AG" = wrong (APPSC 2011).
K.K. Venugopal = AG of the 2017-2022 period (APPSC FRO 2022 key); "the current AG is Mukul Rohatgi" was wrong in 2018 (AG then: Venugopal).

Asked as: SG is "a legal adviser" (UPPSC 1991, 1994); current AG at the time of the exam (Sorabjee 2002; Venugopal for papers of 2018 – Sep 2022; not Rohatgi; from 1 Oct 2022 the AG is R. Venkataramani – a "July 2023" stem naming Venugopal as AG is factually wrong) – check the year, these keys age.

Records (as of 2026): longest-serving Chief Minister = Pawan Kumar Chamling (Sikkim, 1994-2019); on 22 March 2026 Narendra Modi (8,931 days as head of an elected government, CM + PM) passed Chamling's 8,930 (app notes).
"Present CJI" PYQs are dated: key the CJI at the exam date and note the current CJI.

Art. 134(1): appeal as of right when the HC has on appeal reversed an acquittal and sentenced the accused to death, or has withdrawn a case from a subordinate court and convicted and sentenced him to death; otherwise only on HC certificate. No appeal as of right if the HC reverses a conviction.
CAG (Art. 148) and CEC (Art. 324(5)) are removed like an SC judge; Art. 218 applies these provisions to HC judges.

Chief Justice: President after consulting the CJI and the Governor. Other judges: also the Chief Justice of that HC → consultees = HC CJ, CJI, Governor (not the Attorney General). Common HC: Governors of all the States concerned.
V.R. Krishna Iyer was never Chief Justice of India (UPSC 2008: only "progenitor of PIL" is correct). Bhagwati was CJI 1985-86.
AFT trap: Bhopal has an NGT zonal bench, not an AFT bench (APPSC FRO 2025: "as of January 2025").
"Not a federal feature" answers: Office of the Governor (APPSC 2018), CAG (APPSC G2), "result of an agreement among the federating units" (UPSC 2017).

Violating federal principles: Governor, CAG, Emergency powers (esp. Art. 356); Central Services serve only the Union and are not a violation – it is the All India Services (Art. 312) that Laxmikanth says "violate the principle of federalism".
⚠ Sources differ: NextGen prints "Union List 100 subjects"; Laxmikanth 8th ed. gives 98 – the current count.
Art. 52: there shall be a President of India.
Tax sharing is not fixed by the Finance Ministry, RBI, NABARD, NITI Aayog, the Inter-State Council, NDC or the GST Council; the CAG certifies the net proceeds (Art. 279).
Article 280 (Part XII) provides for the Finance Commission (FC), a quasi-judicial constitutional body; Articles 280 and 281 deal with it (Art. 290 = pensions, not the FC; Art. 148 = CAG).
Never FC chairmen: Dr. Manmohan Singh (he was Finance Minister, RBI Governor and at the IMF), Ashok Mehta, Raja Chelliah, T.S. Papola, Y.K. Alagh, Montek Singh.
Divisible pool = gross tax revenue − cesses, surcharges and cost of collection; the CAG certifies net proceeds (Art. 279).
Art. 324(2): the CEC and other ECs are appointed by the President (subject to any law of Parliament) – not elected by Parliament, not appointed by the PM, the Home Minister or the CJI.
CEC and Other ECs (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023 (Act 49 of 2023; replaced the 1991 Act):
Criticism: gives the government a 2:1 majority; challenged by ADR and Jaya Thakur (Jaya Thakur v. Union of India) – pending as of 2026.
new: Criticism: gives the government a 2:1 majority; challenged by ADR and Jaya Thakur (Jaya Thakur v. Union of India) – still pending: on **23 Sep 2026** a two-judge bench split on a larger-bench reference and sent the case to the CJI for a **Constitution Bench** (as of Nov 2026).
why: On 23 Sep 2026 the SC bench (Datta, Sharma JJ) split and the challenge was placed before the CJI for a Constitution Bench.

text: Dinesh Goswami Committee on Electoral Reforms (1990) – appointed by the V.P. Singh Government, chaired by Law Minister Dinesh Goswami; first main recommendation: "Election Commission to be a three-member body", CEC appointed in consultation with the CJI and LoP.

No qualifications and no term prescribed for members; retiring ECs are not debarred from further government appointment (contrast CAG – Art. 148(4), UPSC Chairman – Art. 319). (NextGen's "ineligible for office of profit after retirement" is not a constitutional bar.)

Asked as: who appoints (5 PYQs); how the CEC / an EC is removed (5 PYQs); term 6 years or 65 (statements); equal powers and SC-judge salary; status of the CEC; committee that recommended three members (Goswami); post-retirement bar (APPSC 2024 – false).
Firsts match: Sukumar Sen – first CEC; H.J. Kania – first Chief Justice of India; G.V. Mavalankar – first Speaker of Lok Sabha; M.C. Setalvad – first Attorney General.

Asked as: first CEC (6 PYQs); CEC in a given period (1982-85 Trivedi, 1967-72 Sen Verma, 1990-96 Seshan); "present CEC" (dated – check the exam year); first woman CEC; who was not an EC member; 10th CEC Seshan; Sukumar Sen lecture; firsts match.
Sunil Arora – appointed Election Commissioner in Aug-Sep 2017 (the "newly appointed EC" of 2017 papers); CEC Dec 2018 – Apr 2021.
CEC + such number of ECs as the President fixes; today CEC + 2 ECs = a three-member body (APPSC G2 2025 – "three member body" and "constitutional body" are true; "appointed by the CJI" is false).
The CEC acts as chairman; the President may appoint Regional Commissioners after consulting the Election Commission.
Parliament has no role (unlike SC/HC judges and the CAG, who are removed on an address of both Houses).

Dr. B.R. Ambedkar: the CAG is "the most important officer under the Constitution"; one of the bulwarks of democracy with the Supreme Court, Election Commission and UPSC; auditing both Union and State accounts is a unitary feature.
The CAG is not part of the Union Executive (President, VP, PM, Council of Ministers, Attorney General), nor is the Speaker (part of Parliament).
For the President's election, CAG is an office of profit; the posts of VP, Governor and Minister are not (Art. 58 explanation).
Table of Precedence: CAG is at 9A with the Chairperson UPSC and the Chief Election Commissioner; Chief Justices of High Courts are at 14.

Appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal (Art. 148(1)) – not the PM, FM, UPSC, Parliament or a PM–LoP committee; Attorney General (Art. 76) and Governor (Art. 155) are also appointed by the President.

Term: 6 years or age 65, whichever is earlier (CAG Act, 1971) – the longest among President, VP and Lok Sabha member (5 years). Same as CEC/ECs and UPSC members; SPSC members 6 years or 62; SC judge retires at 65, HC judge at 62 (15th Amendment, 1963: 60 → 62).
Constitution prescribes no qualifications for the CAG; it is a single-member office.

CAG report → President (Union) / Governor (State) under Art. 151 → laid before Parliament / State Legislature → examined by the Public Accounts Committee (PSUs: Committee on Public Undertakings) → Action Taken Notes.
Ultimate action on CAG reports rests with Parliament (not the President, SC or NDC).
Art. 281/151/338: the President must lay before Parliament the FC recommendations, the CAG report and the NCSC report – the PAC report is not laid by him (it goes to the Speaker).
Main function: examine the CAG's audit reports (Appropriation and Finance Accounts) – not day-to-day interference or orders.
CAG = PAC's "friend, philosopher and guide" – he attends its meetings (not the AG or Solicitor General); not of the Estimates Committee or COPU.
No Minister represents the CAG in Parliament (not the Finance Minister).
The CAG has no right to speak, take part or vote in either House or a joint sitting – these Art. 88 rights (speak and take part, no vote) belong to Ministers and the Attorney General.

CAG (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971; 1976 amendment (in force 1 March 1976): accounts separated from audit (departmentalisation) – Union accounts now compiled by the Controller General of Accounts (Finance Ministry), who gives the FM a monthly analytical review; the CAG still keeps most State accounts.
Social audit: CAG laid down the Auditing Standards for Social Audit of MGNREGA (2016).
Paul Appleby criticised the CAG's role and suggested relieving it of audit.

His salary (Art. 112(3)) and the office's expenses (salaries, allowances, pensions of staff) are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India – non-votable (Art. 148(6)); the Attorney General's and Service Chiefs' salaries are not charged.
Service conditions of IA&AD staff and his administrative powers are prescribed by the President after consulting the CAG.
CAG State Finances, AP 2015-16: State's own tax revenue ≈ 45% of total revenue receipts.
CAG State Finances report 2022-23: revenue receipts ₹1,57,768 crore; own tax revenue ₹78,026 crore (about half); own tax 5.92% and central transfers 5.64% of GSDP.
18 Sep 2026: CAG Report No. 31 of 2026 – bio-toilets faulty at 491 of 512 stations; PAC (K.C. Venugopal) pulled up the Railways.
CAG auditing 101 cities for ease of living; AI/ML-based audits to detect welfare fraud; remote audits (Sep 2025).
NITI Aayog (Cabinet resolution, 1 Jan 2015) = extra-constitutional; the odd one among FC, ECI, ISC (UP Lower 2015) and among NCBC, CAG, FC (APPSC 2025).
President appoints AG, FC, CAG, ECI, NCSC, NCST, NCBC, 350B officer.
Order of precedence: UPSC Chairperson, CEC, CAG = 9A; NCM, NCSC, NCST chairpersons = 17.
First CEC Sukumar Sen (1950-58; ECI, not Law Commission); first woman CEC V.S. Ramadevi.
V.S. Ramadevi (Governor, acting CEC) was never NCW chairperson; Smriti Irani and Najma Heptulla were not either.

Appointed by the President on the recommendation of a 6-member committee: PM (head), Speaker of the Lok Sabha, Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, Leaders of the Opposition in both Houses, Union Home Minister. The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Vice-President) is NOT on it.

Asked as: year (1993); not a constitutional body (UPPSC 2007); term (5 years or 70 before 2019 – MPPSC 2018, now 3 years); who is not on the selection committee (RS Chairman – MPPSC 2019); 7th chairperson (H.L. Dattu – APPSC AEE 2016); "current" chairman (Dattu in older papers).
January 2022: the Cabinet extended it by three years beyond 31 Mar 2022, to 31 March 2025; latest extension up to 31 March 2028.

First Chairperson: Justice Ranganath Misra (12 Oct 1993 – 24 Nov 1996); Justice M. Fathima Beevi (first woman SC judge) was one of the first members (1993-97). Present: Justice V. Ramasubramanian (as of Feb 2026).
Secretary-General (Chief Executive Officer of the Commission): administrative and financial powers (not judicial) under the Chairperson's control.
Before 2019: CIC's salary = Chief Election Commissioner, IC = Election Commissioner; State CIC = Election Commissioner, State IC = Chief Secretary; term was 5 years or 65.
Global RTI Rating 2016 (Centre for Law and Democracy and Access Info Europe): India's RTI Act ranked 4th (it slipped to 8th by 2023).
CVCs: K.V. Chowdary (2015-19); Praveen Kumar Srivastava (to 2 Aug 2026); A.S. Rajeev acting CVC from 3 August 2026 (as of 2026).
Bench (2026): judicial member Ritu Raj Awasthi; non-judicial Sushil Chandra (former CEC); wings not fully staffed.
Constitutional body = directly established by the Constitution (EC, FC, CAG, PSCs); statutory = by Act (NHRC, Lokpal, NGT); the Planning Commission was not statutory.
Hung assembly: a pre-poll alliance is treated as one political party; then largest single party, post-poll coalitions.
Asked as: number of national parties (6, as of 2025); "more than 10 national parties" (false); recognition provision in the Constitution (false); symbol not bicycle (RJD); BSP elephant.
AITC got national status on 2 September 2016 – the latest after the 2014 Lok Sabha polls; lost it in April 2023.

Asked as: number of national parties on a date (2019, May 2020); number of State parties (2019); AAP's status (2 PYQs – date-dependent); which is (not) a national party (5 PYQs); latest party to get national status (AITC 2016).

Elections are in Part XV (not XIV, XVI or XVII). Correct pair: ECI – Art. 324 (Supreme Court = 124, UPSC = 315, Attorney General = 76); Art. 280 = Finance Commission; Art. 171 = Legislative Councils, not elections.

ECI set up on 25 January 1950 – permanent constitutional body; its institute IIIDEM trains election managers. Mohinder Singh Gill v CEC (1978): Art. 324 is a "reservoir of power" where Parliament has not legislated.
Shyam Saran Negi (Kalpa, Kinnaur, HP): independent India's first voter (Oct 1951), voted in every general election till 2022; honoured by CEC Navin Chawla (2010).
Delimitation = fixing the number and boundaries of Lok Sabha and Assembly constituencies, and the SC/ST reserved seats, on the latest census – "one person, one vote, one value".
Members (2002 Act): a retired Supreme Court judge (chair), the CEC or an EC he nominates, and the State Election Commissioner – ex officio.
EVM = electronic vote-recording and counting device (not an electoral system). First used: Parur (Kerala), 1982; older EVMs recorded up to 3,840 votes – current ECI EVMs up to 2,000.
Ombudsman for local bodies in AP: the function is entrusted to the Lokayukta (not the CAG or a banking/insurance ombudsman).
Panchayat accounts: the major reported problem is that yearly accounts are not closed in time (CAG / MoPR); hence PRIASoft, eGramSwaraj and AuditOnline.
AP's 13 Zilla Parishads are being reorganised into 28 (one per district) after their terms ended on 24 Sep 2026 (as of 2026).
Official participation of political parties; periodic elections at all levels; elections by the State CEO with the CEC; no supersession – elections within 6 months.
2026: 13 Zilla Praja Parishads reorganised into 28 (one per district); MPTC/ZPTC polls on 5 November 2026; SEC Anil Chandra Punetha ordered photo electoral rolls (as of Nov 2026).
Within a State: among GPs by the latest SFC formula; if none, population 90 : area 10.
Property (house) tax is a local tax and the major own-source revenue of Panchayats (APPSC GS 2018), as of ULBs.
CAG gives only Technical Guidance and Support (TGS) over local-body audit – recommended by the 11th Finance Commission.
Asked as: primary auditor of PRIs (Director, State Audit – not the CAG).
Code trap: "SFC = Article 243" (it is 243I); "SEC appointed by CEC/President" (it is the Governor).
First Vice-Chairman: Arvind Panagariya; then Rajiv Kumar, Suman K. Bery; Ashok Kumar Lahiri from April 2026 (as of 2026).

Meaning: freedom to convert rupees into any major currency (and back) for trading financial assets – investment, loans, portfolio flows (UPSC 1998). Conversion for trade in goods and services = current account convertibility.
Current account: fully convertible since August 1994 (IMF Article VIII obligation).
Other 1991 numbers: fiscal deficit about 9.4% of GDP, inflation about 12%, GDP growth only about 1.3%.

FSDC (Financial Stability and Development Council), 2010: non-statutory apex body (executive order), not an organ of NITI Aayog; chaired by the Union Finance Minister (not RBI Governor); sub-committee chaired by the RBI Governor. Proposed by the Raghuram Rajan Committee (2008).
Roles: financial stability, inter-regulatory coordination, macro-prudential supervision, financial literacy and inclusion – not fixing the repo rate.
Virtual courts: 21 virtual courts in 17 States/UTs (as of 31 January 2023) – online disposal of traffic challans under eCourts Phase II.
CAG found that the Social Audit Unit lacks functional independence.
Angles: MGNREGA accountability process (×2), who conducts it (Gram Sabha), SSAAT, CAG finding, training days.
TRAI Chairpersons: J.S. Sharma (2009-12, the answer in older papers) … R.S. Sharma (2015-20), P.D. Vaghela (2020-23); Anil Kumar Lahoti from January 2024 (as of 2026).

Reports of the CAG (Art. 151), UPSC (Art. 323) and National Commission for SCs (Art. 338) must be laid before Parliament under the Constitution; the Atomic Energy Commission (an executive body) has no such requirement.
